    <item>
      <title>Coupling of TQFTs to QFTs and SymTFT interfaces from bordisms</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25012</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25012v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: M-theory local models may exhibit torsional cycles and other non-trivial topology which interpolate between quantum field theory sectors localized at singularities and the asymptotic regions of the local model. We show that such structures give rise, in standard decoupling limits, to additional topological sectors which can couple non-trivially to the localized QFT. From a symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) perspective, the physical boundary conditions associated to such local models are modified. We give a construction of SymTFT interfaces from geometric bordisms interpolating between the local singularity and the asymptotic boundary. We apply this construction to the circle compactification of a frozen $D_5$ singularity, identifying a topological interface between the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ SymTFT of the full theory and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ SymTFT of its local $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ gauge sector. We show that the resulting coupling between the gauge theory and an additional topological quantum field theory accounts for the apparent mismatch between electric and magnetic symmetries of the frozen theory.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25014</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25014v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25017</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25017v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Asymmetric Orbifolds and 4-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ String Islands</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25020</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25020v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We formulate heterotic and type II $\mathbb T^6/\mathbb Z_n$ asymmetric orbifolds preserving all 16 right-moving supersymmetries and leading to 4-dimensional islands without massless moduli other than the dilaton. We establish the consistency of the orbifold conformal field theory, including the validity of operator interpretation. In the heterotic case we classify all islands based on the $\Gamma(22,6)$ lattice constructed via the Leech lattice. In the type II case we also provide a classification of allowed $\Gamma(6,6)$ lattices and orbifold generators. In both cases we further examine whether a particular orbifold admits an archipelago of different islands arising from inequivalent realizations of the orbifold action.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Conformal manifolds of $\mathcal{N}=1$ orbifold theories - Part I: Marginal deformations and the one-loop spectrum</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25021</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25021v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider orbifolds of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory that preserve minimal supersymmetry and study their conformal manifolds, focusing on two families of Abelian orbifolds in the planar limit. We compute their superconformal indices, construct their complete single-trace BPS spectra and identify the conformal manifolds. These are generically spanned by a subset of the gauge-couplings, whose number we derive from both gauge and string theory, and a universal Leigh--Strassler-type superpotential deformation. We then construct the complete, planar one-loop dilatation operator on these conformal manifolds, giving perturbative access to the full non-BPS spectrum away from the orbifold point. This lays the groundwork for studying special loci of the conformal manifold in a forthcoming Part II.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Stringy Corrections from Gravity: Predictions for BFSS and ABJM</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25022</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25022v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite enormous progress in string theory, the leading stringy corrections to many holographic observables remain unknown. String/M-theory dualities nonetheless allow them to be determined from gravity alone. From the winding modes of one-loop 11d supergravity on a circle, we derive the leading tree-level stringy terms in the type IIA effective action for the metric, dilaton, and Ramond--Ramond one-form, in closed form as a finite supertrace over Lorentz generators. On the thermal D0-brane geometry, this gives the first correction to the low-temperature thermodynamics of the BFSS matrix model. Its coefficient differs from published lattice Monte Carlo estimates by $\approx 20\%$. With the four-form flux included, the same method reproduces the $\zeta(3)k^{2}$ term of the ABJM free energy on the three-sphere obtained by localization.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Actionless Branes on Axion Wormholes</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25026</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25026v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can a Euclidean axion wormhole extend to infinity with every instanton still suppressed? The imaginary distance bound says it cannot: some instanton must become actionless first. Calabi-Yau compactifications appear to violate the bound: several axions share the field excursion, and the instantons charged under any one of them stay suppressed all the way. We show that the wormhole can hide from these instantons but not from their bound states: misaligned central charges make a bound state cheaper than its constituents, while the axions act on every constituent. On the type IIB wormhole supported by two axions of the Neveu-Schwarz two-form, a fivebrane carrying string charge becomes actionless at large volume within two thirds of the way to infinity, for either relative sign of the axions and however they share the excursion. In S-dual variables it is a D5-brane with magnetic flux for one sign and a D5-NS5 bound state for the other. Adding more axions does not help: the same branes become actionless on every Calabi-Yau threefold, because what counts is the degree of homogeneity of the saxion sector, not the number of axions. These bound states are what the convex-hull axion weak gravity conjecture requires.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Twist and Shout: defect lines on the R\'enyi torus</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25032</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25032v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider what the entanglement between two regions of a critical system can reveal about its symmetries, including non-invertible ones. For two intervals in a two-dimensional conformal field theory, the second R\'enyi entropy is a partition function on a torus, and a topological defect line can be wrapped around one of the intervals. For an on-site symmetry this computes the overlap of the reduced density matrix with its image under the symmetry acting on one interval, and in general it defines an observable that depends only on the cross-ratio. As the intervals approach each other, the observable vanishes at a rate set by the lightest operator on which the line can end, and its monodromy is fixed by the spins of such operators. Since these spins are constrained by the fusion category, the observable detects 't Hooft anomalies and distinguishes categories with the same fusion rules. It can be computed in closed form for a $\mathbb{Z}_2$, a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and a Fibonacci line of the $(E_8)_1$ theory, and for the spin-flip and Kramers-Wannier lines of the Ising model, where the spin-flip result agrees with an exact computation in the critical Ising chain. Averaged over a symmetry, the observable reduces to a known Jones-index bound on the mutual information. We also show that the associated twist-field crossing equations are a form of the modular bootstrap, and discuss whether the full fusion category can be recovered from entanglement on surfaces of higher genus.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Entanglement entropy from fundamental strings</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25045</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25045v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In previous work, we derived the local entropy capacity from off-shell string theory and combined it with the gravitational replica construction and flow-cut duality to normalize the entropy flow carried by physical fundamental strings. In this paper, we apply this framework to interval entanglement in holographic CFT$_2$. We construct explicit on-shell F1 worldsheets in the AdS$_3$ vacuum and planar BTZ, derive their Kalb-Ramond source currents, and show that the normalized spatial currents saturate the corresponding RT surface. Their flux reproduces both the vacuum single interval entropy and the finite temperature CFT$_2$ result. We then vary the NS-NS flux fraction. Although the total maximal flux remains unchanged, the F1 equations continuously redistribute the strings among different parts of the complement. In planar BTZ, the resulting signed flux through the bifurcation line reproduces the extensive thermal entropy and can vanish in the pure NS-NS limit without changing the interval entropy. Thus the on-shell string dynamics additionally determines its physical routing and boundary contact structure.</description>

    <item>
      <title>$C_T$ and $C_J$ of general scalar--fermion conformal field theories in $d=4-\epsilon$</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25055</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25055v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We compute $C_T$ and $C_J$, the coefficients of the stress-tensor and conserved-current two-point functions, to order $\epsilon^3$ at any fixed point of the general renormalizable theory of scalars and fermions in $d=4-\epsilon$. We give explicit results for the chiral Ising, XY and Heisenberg models and for fixed points with emergent supersymmetry in $d=3$. In theories without a four-dimensional counterpart, fermion loops with an odd number of Yukawa vertices contribute at order $\epsilon^3$ through traces whose continuation away from $d=3$ is ambiguous; we fix it with $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry, by computing the two-point functions of the supercurrent and of the fermionic partner of a flavor current to four loops. In $d=3$, Pad\'e approximants closely reproduce the exact $C_T$ of the $\mathcal N=2$ super-Ising model. We estimate the universal conductivity at the charge-density-wave, Kekul\'e and N\'eel transitions of graphene to be $\sigma/\sigma_{\rm free}\approx0.91$, $0.79$--$0.83$ and $0.64$--$0.74$, and show that the exact conductivity at the supersymmetric transition on the surface of a topological insulator is $\sigma/\sigma_{\rm free}=\frac{9}{10}\,C_T/C_{T,\rm free}\approx0.654$, $10\%$ below the value previously reported.</description>

      <title>Nonzero cubic Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25059</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25059v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Static Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes vanish at linear and quadratic order in General Relativity, while generic nonlinear tides remain less understood. We solve a specific non-axisymmetric octupolar tide at cubic order and, building on the symmetry of static General Relativity exploited by Parra-Martinez and Podo, match the result to a worldline effective field theory (EFT) using dimensional regularization. Surprisingly, we find a Love number that neither vanishes nor runs.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Soft Factorisation of WQFT and the Spinning 4PM Magnusian</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25090</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25090v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive the soft divergences of $\hat{N}=-i\log\hat{S}$ in the Worldline Quantum Field Theory (WQFT) formalism, focusing on poles due to single massive-massive (Coulomb) and massive-massless (tail) graviton exchanges. Our derivation is inspired by the Faddeev-Kulish procedure, switching the interaction picture to one with an infrared-finite $\hat{N}$-matrix. Soft divergences emerging from the worldline are correlators of Wilson lines. As confirmation of this structure, we demonstrate explicitly how divergences of inclusive observables including the momentum impulse $\Delta p_i^\mu$ and spin kick $\Delta S_i^\mu$ cancel, and we reproduce the infrared divergence of the one-loop scattering waveform. Using the Magnus series representation of $\hat{N}$ and Murua coefficients, we then calculate the Magnusian $N=\langle0|\hat{N}|0\rangle$ at fourth post-Minkowskian (4PM) order, including linear-in-spin corrections. For aligned spins, $-\partial N/\partial L$ reproduces the full scattering angle through 3PM order; at 4PM order, $N$ develops a soft divergence as predicted by our soft factorisation. Using the Feynman $i0^+$ prescription, we also derive an infrared-finite 4PM Magnusian which compactly encodes existing results for the conservative momentum impulse and spin kick via nested iterations of Poisson brackets.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Calabi-Yau linear models with abelian bundles</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25101</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25101v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a construction of (0,2) gauged linear sigma models whose large radius phases realize Calabi-Yau sigma models with line bundles. We study a family of such models admitting Landau-Ginzburg orbifold phases, described as asymmetric orbifolds of (2,2) Gepner models and free left-moving fermions. These orbifolds extend the Gepner construction to a broader class of (0,2) SCFTs, and reveal unexpected features, including the emergence of free fermions in twisted sectors and substantial enhancements of the left-moving current algebra. The gauged linear sigma model connects the Calabi-Yau geometry to these rational points, where the volume modulus becomes charged under the enhanced gauge symmetry and freezes at the string scale.</description>

    <item>
      <title>From Instantons to AdS Boundaries: Tracing the Geometric Path from Quantum Anomalies to Massive Gravity</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25103</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This thesis studies how boundary data enter two gravitational observables: the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in three-dimensional New Massive Gravity. In Einstein gravity coupled to ModMax electrodynamics, we compute the index of charged Dirac fermions on Taub-NUT and Eguchi-Hanson instantons using the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer theorem, which includes the spectral asymmetry of the boundary Dirac operator. The Taub-NUT index agrees with the Maxwell result. For Eguchi-Hanson, the gauge-field contribution to the axial anomaly depends explicitly on the ModMax parameter when expressed in terms of the solution parameters. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter solutions of New Massive Gravity with Brown-Henneaux boundary conditions, a term linear in the extrinsic curvature reproduces the holographic stress tensor of the auxiliary-field formulation. At the degenerate point, relaxed boundary conditions admit an additional constrained Fefferman-Graham coefficient. A quadratic extrinsic counterterm cancels the residual power divergence. We derive the boundary Ward identity and show that the holographic and Noether-Wald charges agree for the solutions studied.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Holographic Duals of $SL^{(q)}(2, \mathbb{R})$ Deformed CFTs</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25240</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25240v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the holographic bulk dual of 2D CFTs evolved by $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed Hamiltonians. Working in the Hamiltonian-adapted frame, in which the $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed effective Floquet Hamiltonian generates time translations, we construct the dual Ba\~nados geometries for the three distinct classes of dynamics: the heating phase, the non-heating phase and the phase boundary. Specifically, we show that in the heating phase, the bulk patch dual to the region between two neighbouring fixed points has a time-dependent causal horizon and asymptotes to a static AdS Rindler geometry at late times, while the non-heating phase has no horizon. We discuss how the late-time behaviour of the entanglement entropy, particularly its linear growth in the heating phase, can be understood from the bulk in two different ways: in global AdS, from the portion of the geodesic behind the horizons, and in a quotient description, from an effective shockwave produced by a boosted conical defect. Finally, for ($q=1$), we complete the holographic analysis of Ref. [1] by reproducing the exact CFT expression of the OTOC from the bulk and explaining why it exhibits an exponential growth {\it only} when the operators lie on the side of the two fixed points.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25473</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25473v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim \bar\phi^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2\nu\bar\phi}$) bulk potentials, where $\bar\phi$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n\to\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. For the exponential model, we derive analytically the bound $R_{11}<1$, with the largest value approached for the case $\nu\to 1^+$ (where $\nu=1$ corresponds to the linear dilaton model) and consistent with unitarity sum rules. For exponential models we also obtain the absolute upper bound on the second radion mode ratio $R_{21}=m_{r_2}/m_{h_1}\lesssim 1.374$. This value is reached for $\nu=2$ when the IR brane approaches the singularity. For this configuration, we verify that the scalar contribution satisfies the unitarity sum rule when the complete radion Kaluza-Klein tower is included.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25507</link>
      <description>arXiv:2611.25507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.</description>
